Subject: Re: [PATCH] t/comp/opsubs.t

On Tue, Nov 13, 2007 at 08:44:40PM -0500, Jarkko Hietaniemi wrote:
> Gerard Goossen wrote:
> > On Mon, Nov 12, 2007 at 04:13:58PM -0500, Jarkko Hietaniemi wrote:
> >> With miniperl the test failed:
> >>
> >> ./miniperl -T -Ilib t/comp/opsubs.t.dist
> >>
> > [...]
> >>  
> >> +BEGIN {
> >> +    chdir 't' if -d 't';
> >> +    @INC = '../lib';
> >> +}
> > 
> > Isn't TestInit there to replace that? And shouldn't you use -MTestInit
> > on your command line?
> 
> TestInit is currently used by, let me see, zero t/*/*.t tests.
> It is used by t/TEST.  Using it in the above command line makes
> no difference since the issue was that the test failed with make
> minitest.  And I think any test should behave identically regardless
> of whether it is run manually with the minimum of options or via t/TEST
> or via t/harness (unless, of course, the test tests exactly how it has
> been run...)

That t/TEST uses makes it for me the standard to use. But just before a release
might not the ideal time to start introduction using 'use TestInit'.
So just for my information, for what I do with kurila or for 5.11: Should we
use TestInit, wouldn't using TestInit also make it easy to run the test on an already
installed perl.

> 
> >> +
> >>  use warnings;
> >>  use strict;
> >>  $|++;
> >>  
> >> +require "./test.pl";
> > 
> > I don't think it is a problem here, but I prefer this 'require' in a BEGIN 
> > block ('ok' and 'is' are often assumed prototyped).
> > 
> >> +
> >> +plan(tests => 36);
> >> +
> >> +use vars qw($TODO);
> > 
> > please don't use vars, especially not in such a basic test like t/comp/opsubs.t
> 
> I can instead do voodoo like
> 
> $TODO = $TODO;
>
> but I need some way to make use strict happy since the $TODO is used
> later in the file.

Or just C

> I don't know how use vars is any worse than use
> strict or *shudder* use warnings.

I agree, and they also should not be used.

-- 
Gerard Goossen
TTY Internet Solutions
